label: Week ahead: a plan from the calendar, the Red folder record, the tested calendar rules and the desk's levels. Not advice, not a forecast; paper only.
lines: A short week: US markets closed Thursday, early close Friday. Expect thin trading around the holiday.
Prediction markets on the 9 Dec Fed decision: Kalshi Hike 25bps 90%, Polymarket 25 bps increase 90%. What traders pay, not a forecast of ours.
Before the print: PCE (Wednesday): the Cleveland Fed nowcast for October is core +0.27%, headline +0.31% month on month (as of 2026-11-20), a model's estimate, not the consensus.
Priced on a prediction market for this week's prints (Wednesday: core PCE for October 2026: most likely +0.3% (87%)). What traders pay: not a consensus survey and not a forecast of ours.

From the 2022-24 first-print record: PCE (Wednesday): Core CPI for October printed 0.30% m/m (the Cleveland Fed's file of actual prints, read 2026-11-20). On the 2022-24 record a core CPI of 0.3% went with core PCE near 0.24% (fit on 36 months, typical miss ±0.07 pp): a descriptive fit on past months, not a forecast on the record.
The US data that move gold most: PCE (Wednesday).
Calendar rules the desk has tested that passed their bar: Wednesday: the last trading day before a US market holiday and a gotobi day. Paper only, each with its own forward record: not proven.
Rules tested and failed also fall on Friday: listed there so they are not chased.

hard.title: How the last Treasury auctions went
lines: 19 Nov 9-Year 8-Month TIPS (reopening), $19bn: high yield 2.903%, bid-to-cover 2.43 (the 2 before averaged 2.27), indirect bidders took 69% (62% before), dealers took 6%. Stronger demand than the earlier ones.
18 Nov 20-Year Bond, $16bn: high yield 5.459%, bid-to-cover 2.63 (the 3 before averaged 2.61), indirect bidders took 60% (58% before), dealers took 13%.
12 Nov 30-Year Bond, $25bn: high yield 5.441%, bid-to-cover 2.36 (the 3 before averaged 2.51), indirect bidders took 68% (73% before), dealers took 11%. Softer demand than the earlier ones.
10 Nov 10-Year Note, $42bn: high yield 5.020%, bid-to-cover 2.46 (the 3 before averaged 2.67), indirect bidders took 61% (79% before), dealers took 10%. Softer demand than the earlier ones.
Bid-to-cover = bids for each dollar sold; indirect bidders are mostly foreign and institutional buyers. Weak demand can lift yields. Context, not a signal.
